batch: Physical origins for typed analysis-card errors

environment.cli_toolchain_reason: Previously reproduced pinned Rust 1.94/faer compiler crash in CLI runtime builds; repository pin unchanged.

commands.command: cargo clippy --locked -p rspice-core -p rspice-cli -p rspice-wasm -p rspice-engine-adapter -p rspice-python --lib --bins --test analysis_error_origins -- -D warnings

cargo test --locked -p rspice-core --target wasm32-unknown-unknown --release --no-default-features --features wasm,veriloga-wasm-jit --test analysis_error_origins --test forward_analyses -- --nocapture

test_accounting: 1096 netlist unit tests, 21 public core integration tests, four Python attribute-projection unit tests and one CLI integration test. Earlier development runs and publication-ledger checks are excluded.
source_hash_format: SHA-256 of committed Git blob bytes
implementation: AnalysisCardError retains an optional physical NetlistSourceLocation while keeping the public card, line and issue. Its constructor preserves the existing unattributed line-only behavior; source_location supplies the physical owner when available.

Parser source attribution attaches a physical origin once and keeps the error typed. Repeated source-map passes do not remap an included error onto its caller. Deferred root and scoped cards use the same attribution boundary.

ParseError::source_location and Display expose the physical card location. Python SDK attribute projection preserves the source and primary_source fields. CLI check retains the corrected physical line and message path.
Core README documents the added field for SDK struct-literal callers and recommends the compatible constructor.
acceptance_evidence: Root and subcircuit failures after forward binding preserve AnalysisCard::Pss and the InvalidNumber issue for HARMS.
Authenticated sealed source bundles exercise two include levels and continuation lines without filesystem fallback on native and optimized WASM builds.
Missing-field, unknown-keyword, duplicate-keyword and invalid-number failures retain source-local card lines and included paths, including scoped pending cards.
In-memory errors and direct constructors retain line-only locations and existing display wording. An idempotence unit test preserves an already attributed included error.
CLI check JSON reports the physical card line and includes the physical path in its message. Python projections expose the same origin in existing source attributes.
limits: This batch covers typed analysis-card diagnostic ownership; it does not redesign generic syntax/value-error metadata or all frontend error envelopes.
TEMP/TNOM options that close before later parent declarations, and provisional ngspice temperature-domain errors, remain open.
These focused parsing and propagation checks do not replace full numerical/model/control/performance qualification. No C00-C14 package is closed.
No selected tests are ignored. The full-suite ignored-test inventory remains unchanged from prior evidence.

One CLI rebuild failed in the compiler before tests ran. A passing retry does not prove compiler-build reproducibility; the earlier Rust 1.94/faer incident and this Rust 1.95 assembler diagnostic remain C14 toolchain qualification work.
development_notes: The first compile exposed a missing AST import and a thiserror formatting expression, both corrected before validation. The first public source-path assertion compared Windows slash spellings rather than path identity; corrected the message assertion while keeping the exact structured path check. Final selected checks use the committed implementation; the WASM build started from the same unchanged implementation files immediately before commit.

compiler_incidents.diagnostic: expected relocatable expression while compiling rspice-core
compiler_incidents.follow_up: The same command passed after the other local qualification chain completed. No source, toolchain or compiler-setting workaround was applied. The successful retry is recorded separately above; build reproducibility remains unqualified.

publication_validation.scope: Ledger and evidence-path validation after the documentation edits; excluded from unique implementation test counts.
